Evanescent

ev-uh-NES-uhnt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Evanescent is quickly fading or disappearing.

The northern lights offered an evanescent display that vanished before most tourists could reach their cameras.

Worked Example

The morning fog over the lake was evanescent, burning away completely within the first hour of sunlight.

Evanescent describes something beautiful or striking that exists only briefly before fading away completely, like fog, a rainbow, or a brief, passing feeling.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fleeting: lasting only a very short time

ephemeral: lasting for a very brief time

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

permanent: lasting forever or for a very long time

enduring: continuing to exist over a long period

Where it sits · how fast it is gone — brief → evanescent → instantaneous

brief vs. evanescent: Something brief simply doesn't last long; it may still be noticed clearly while it happens.

instantaneous vs. evanescent: Something instantaneous happens and vanishes in literally an instant, an even shorter span than something evanescent.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — e-

prefix — e-: out (Latin (ex-))

root — van

root — van: empty, vain (Latin (vanus))

suffix — -escent

suffix — -escent: becoming (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: e- ("out") + van ("empty") + -escent ("becoming") = becoming empty -- fading out of existence.

Use the root in a new word: vanish

Use the root in a new word: vanish: The same root gives us "vanish," the everyday word for disappearing completely, which is almost exactly what something evanescent does.

Word Choice

Evanescent is a literary, almost delicate word -- it fits describing something beautiful and brief, like light, mist, or a feeling, more than something merely short in duration.
